title: Universal derivation of the principal quotient Roos functor on K-flat complexes
statement: On a site essentially small in the coefficient universe, let R be a sheaf of commutative rings and t a global section. If countable products of R-module sheaves are exact, the ordinary quotient Roos functor [def-pur-principal-quotient-completion-model] admits a universal left derived functor whose counit is invertible on every K-flat cochain complex [def-pc-kflat-complex]. No augmentation or completion unit is part of this assertion.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 0941; the indicated explicit steps of lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange.

proof.text: Use Mathlib mapBifunctorMapHomotopy₂ in the variable complex. Prove its naturality in the fixed quotient complex by testing on total-tensor summand inclusions and applying naturality of the underlying tensor bifunctor. These components assemble into a homotopy in the strict tower category. Apply roosF_homotopy_functor and DerivedCategory.Q_map_eq_of_homotopy to descend quotientRoos followed by Q through the homotopy quotient.

For a quasi-isomorphism f between arbitrary K-flat complexes X and Y, resolve each fixed quotient complex B by a K-flat complex K with p:K→B. The signed-total-tensor theorem makes p tensor X, p tensor Y, and K tensor f quasi-isomorphisms. Naturality of tensor gives their commuting square, and two-out-of-three proves B tensor f a quasi-isomorphism. Evaluation detects quasi-isomorphisms in the strict tower category. No flat-term hypothesis on X or Y is needed.

Exact countable products make roosPmap of a tower quasi-isomorphism a quasi-isomorphism, using the existing HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_limMap from WeilConjectures.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TowerLimit. Apply DerivedCategory.Q to the natural map between the two cone triangles for roosU. The two product components are invertible, so the cone component is invertible. Reflect this to a cone quasi-isomorphism and shift by -1 to obtain a quasi-isomorphism of the actual roosF complexes.

K-flat cochain resolutions give a resolving class of homotopy-category objects. Fullness of the homotopy quotient represents each arrow between class objects by a chain map, so the previous invariance proves the class hypothesis. Use quasiIso_saturated_triangulated for right fractions and two-out-of-three, resolvingClass_essentialConstancy for denominator cones, and leftDerived_defined_pointwiseKan_bridge for pointwise Kan extensions. Assemble totalLeftDerived and its universal counit. Compare the canonical pointwise limit cone with the denominator cone at the identity stage to prove the counit invertible on every class object.

Precompose the pointwise Kan extension with the full, essentially surjective homotopy quotient. Its induced functors on structured-arrow categories are initial, so restriction preserves the defining limits. Transport the cones along quotientCompQhIso and the factorization isomorphism of Quotient.lift. This gives the precise cochain counit and universal property in the statement. Each new counit component is the old class component composed with isomorphisms, so all K-flat computation assertions follow.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YM, 06YP, 06YS, 06YT and 0941; Tag 06XN (dual resolving-class argument). R3: explicit tensor-homotopy naturality, exact-product cone argument, and pointwise Kan transport to the cochain quotient.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_derivedQuotientRoos
    (t : (SheafOfModules.unit
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)).sections)
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ)
      (ringedSiteModules.{r} (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R))] :
    ∃ (L : DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{r}
        (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)) ⥤
        DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{r}
          (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)))
      (ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ L ⟶ quotientRoos R t ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q),
      L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)) ∧
        ∀ P, CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := R) P →
          IsIso (ε.app P)
